main_text.l: HAving evidenced that one of Satan's principal designs is a-
gainst the Peace and Comfort of God's Children; I shall
next endeavour a discovery of the various ways by which he doth
undermine them herein. All inward troubles are not of the same
kind in themselves, neither doth Satan always produce the same
effects out of all. Some being in their own nature disquiets, that
do not so directly, and immediately overthrow the Peace and Joy
of believing, and the Comforts of assurance of Divine Favour, as
others do. Yet seeing that by all, he hath no small advantage
against us, as to Sin and Trouble, and that any of them at the long-
run, may lead us to question our interest in Grace, and the Love of
God, and may accordingly afflict us, I shall speak of them all;
which that I may do the more distinctly, I shall rank these trou-
bles into several heads, under peculiar names, (it may be not alto-
gether so proper, but that the curious may find matter of excepti-
on to them) that by them and their explanation, the differen-
ces may the better appear. I distinguish therefore of a fourfold
